# ICS PDF — tiny synthetic fixture, foreign-currency row

`ics-sample-tiny-foreign.pdf` is the sibling of
[`ics-sample-tiny.pdf`](ics-sample-tiny.md), generated by the same
script and in the same hand-crafted PDF 1.4 byte sequence. Everything
in that record applies here — generator, generator choice,
reproducibility, and the canonical anonymisation placeholders — and
only the transaction row differs.

NOT a real ICS export.

## Generator

```sh
php scripts/generate_tiny_ics_pdf.php
```

The script writes both fixtures in one run and is idempotent.

## Synthetic content

```
15 april 2026
KAARTHOUDER ****-****-****-XXXX
Vorig openstaand saldo  EUR 0,00
Totaal ontvangen betalingen  EUR 0,00
Totaal nieuwe uitgaven  EUR 43,71
Nieuw openstaand saldo  EUR 43,71
Bestedingslimiet  EUR 100,00
Minimaal te betalen bedrag  EUR 43,71
12 apr. 12 apr. SYNTHETIC ICS FOREIGN  50,00 USD  43,71  Af
Wisselkoers USD  1,14390
```

The row is the two-column foreign shape `ics-sample-1.txt` records
empirically: the figure the merchant billed (`50,00 USD`) in the
`Bedrag in vreemde valuta` column, the figure the card moved by
(`43,71`) in the `Bedrag in euro's` column, the `Af` direction marker
at the end, and the `Wisselkoers` line the parser reads
`rawPayload.fxRateDisplayed` from. Parsed, it is one row of
`-5000 USD` native and `-4371 EUR` settled.

## Why it exists

`Receipts/tests/Contracts/FingerprintParityTest` held one ICS pair and
it was a domestic EUR row — the one case where the native and settled
legs are the same figure, so it holds however either source denominates
them. The receipt-mail matcher booked a foreign charge's settled leg in
the FOREIGN currency while this adapter read the euro column, and
nothing caught it. This fixture is the twin source the
`ics foreign` pair needs; its receipt half is
`Modules/Receipts/tests/fixtures/ics/foreign-currency-receipt.eml`,
deliberately aligned on merchant, amounts and booked date.
